content:
Let the distance between adjacent pegs be \(1\) unit.

### 1. Area of quadrilateral I
Draw the horizontal diagonal joining its two middle vertices. Its length is \(2\), and the top and bottom vertices are each \(1\) unit from this diagonal. Thus, quadrilateral I is divided into two triangles, each with base \(2\) and height \(1\):

\[
A_I=2\left(\frac12\cdot 2\cdot 1\right)=2.
\]

### 2. Area of quadrilateral II
Draw the horizontal segment from the left-middle vertex to the center vertex. This segment has length \(1\). The top-right and bottom vertices are each \(1\) unit from it, so:

\[
A_{II}=2\left(\frac12\cdot 1\cdot 1\right)=1.
\]

Therefore,

\[
A_I=2>1=A_{II}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\text{A: The area of quadrilateral I is more than the area of quadrilateral II.}}
\]
